facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against the cautious view is deleveraging and diversification of ownership: the IPO repaid USD 780.3 million of term loan, five of six directors are independent, the sponsor is selling rather than adding to its stake, and backlog and awarded contracts rose 92.49% year on year. The view would improve if the material weaknesses are remediated and attested for 2026, if book-to-bill returns to 1.5x, and if the new buyback is funded from cash flow rather than borrowing. It would worsen if the sponsor sells down further and the credit agreement treats a change of control as a default, or if acquisitions continue to be paid for with the term loan. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage is moderate, but financial policy has turned from repayment to growth and returns, and the sponsor's pledged stake adds control risk. Net leverage fell from 8.79x at FY2024 to 2.27x at 2026-09-30 (2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01) after the IPO repaid USD 780.3 million of term loan, but the group has since drawn a USD 200.0 million incremental term loan, completed three acquisitions and authorised a USD 150.0 million buyback. The credit agreement also lets the borrower add pari passu debt, subject to conditions, while first lien net leverage is no greater than 5.25x and, by management's estimate at 2025-12-31, about USD 1.4 billion of junior secured and USD 1.5 billion of unsecured debt, so the current ratio does not bind financial policy. Blackstone-linked holders owned about 61% of the votes in March 2026 and an indicative 46.67% in November 2026 on share-count arithmetic, they have pledged all their shares, and the tax receivable agreement and sponsor-linked lenders align cash and votes with the sponsor rather than with creditors. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against the cautious view is that deleveraging and cash generation are reported, not forecast: net leverage fell to 2.27x (2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01), last-twelve-month free cash flow was 98.18% of reported EBITDA, two agencies upgraded the company in June 2026, and the average relationship with the ten largest clients is 23 years with no client above 10% of revenue. Those facts lower single-name risk and make a quick liquidity squeeze unlikely. The view would improve if book-to-bill stays above 1.0x while the data-centre share stops rising, if working-capital float persists without acquired help, if the control weaknesses are remediated, and if the buyback is paid from free cash flow. It would worsen if revolver usage passed USD 70.0 million, if book-to-bill fell below 1.0x, if the sponsor's margin lenders forced a sale of its controlling block, or if reported net leverage rose back toward 3.83x. facts.text: Margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure but not under a sharp project slowdown. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Buyer power is high on large projects because contracts are fixed-price, work is often subcontracted through general contractors and architects, and clients can reduce or terminate contracts at any time, offset by long relationships and no client above 10% of revenue. Supplier power is low for equipment and materials, which come from many vendors, with tariffs and equipment costs passed to clients, but high for scarce skilled labour, where shortages could raise wages and third-party costs. facts.label: Macro and policy factors
facts.text: Three outside factors change the credit view. Interest rates and the construction cycle drive client capital budgets and the cost of the floating-rate term loan, so rate moves reach cash flow through both the hedge expiry on 2026-12-31 and client demand. Trade policy and tariffs raise material costs and delay supply; the issuer says tariffs on internationally procured materials are passed to clients, which protects margins but can slow projects. Technology investment in data centers, and the availability of water or other utility services at their sites, set the pace of the largest end market. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: The financial profile is adequate and improving. The main supports are moderate leverage (2.27x reported, 2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01), cash generation of 98.18% of reported EBITDA, and covered near-term calls. The main constraints are revenue concentration, thin reported earnings (a 6.99% margin), acquisition-driven leverage and sponsor-linked claims. The trend is better on leverage and interest cover, which rose to 5.28x on reported EBITDA, and worse on concentration, which rose from 39.2% to 62.6% in a year. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C21; calculation C16

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over three to five years the outlook depends on how long data-centre and life-science construction stays strong, because that decides how much of the installed work turns into repeat maintenance revenue, and on how sponsor ownership evolves before the 2030 revolver and 2031 term loan maturities. No management guidance or sector forecast is supplied, so this horizon is not established beyond the issuer's own risk statements. Sector tailwinds are technology investment and building-efficiency demand; headwinds are utility constraints at data-centre sites, tariffs, skilled labour shortages and higher rates. Company tailwinds are backlog, bonding access and acquisition integration; company headwinds are the sponsor's pledged stake, the tax receivable agreement and the shift of policy toward the buyback. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The realistic downside starts with data-centre clients deferring projects, for example because utility services such as water are unavailable at a site or because a client's own capital budget is cut. The first operational break is slower backlog conversion on fixed-price new-building work, where most performance comes late in a project, with the labour force and fabrication capacity already in place; book-to-bill falling below 1.0x would confirm it. Revenue and installation margins fall together, and because wages are the largest cost and many employees are unionised, costs adjust slowly. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: Leverage is the slower channel. Reported EBITDA would have to fall 33.07% before pro forma net leverage of 2.56x returned to the 3.83x of FY2025, and the springing test applies only if revolver usage passes USD 70.0 million, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in a moderate slowdown. A change of control would add a further call, because the tax receivable agreement ends early on one and requires a termination payment whose amount is not stated. A severe, prolonged freeze combined with a sponsor margin-loan default, a loss of the rating-linked margin step-down and weak integration of acquired businesses would be needed to threaten debt service, and the observable triggers are book-to-bill below 1.0x, revolver usage rising, negative working-capital cash flow and a sponsor sale. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Legence presents an adequate business profile supported by backlog, long client relationships and bonding access, but credit quality is constrained by data-centre concentration, acquisition-led growth, thin reported earnings and sponsor-linked claims on cash. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow was 98.18% of reported EBITDA, though it depends on working-capital float. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the data-centre cycle, the ratings that underpin the margin step-down and the covenant staying untested; no large debt maturity falls due before 2030. The primary downside path is a pause in data-centre construction that reverses working-capital float while acquisition and sponsor claims keep cash leaving. Against typical leveraged building-services issuers the profile cannot be ranked because no peer data is supplied. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, the rating levels, revenue by client, and the earnings and net debt of acquired businesses. Top risk: concentration in one end market funded in part by acquisitions. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; calculation C21

## Request

Source readiness for Legence Corp. (lgn-2052568), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: whether the five supplied filings support the requested source readiness, financial foundation, business and governance, and fundamental credit work, and what they cannot support. No credit conclusion is drawn here.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied filings support a credit snapshot of Legence Corp. as at the third quarter of 2026, with limitations, so the requested analysis can proceed on filed statements alone. They do not carry the executed credit agreement, the rating levels or dated market prices, so any covenant, rating or pricing statement is bounded to what management disclosed.

The newest filing was signed on 2026-11-12, 6 days before the as-of date and 43 days after the quarter ended on 2026-09-30. Two events fall after that quarter end, the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01 and the buyback authorised on 2026-11-10, and later work must treat them as subsequent events, not as quarter figures. The 2025 prospectus predates the latest term loan and revolver amendments, so it is background for debt terms only.

spans.text: # Financial foundation for Legence Corp. (lgn-2052568)
## Request

Financial foundation for Legence Corp. (lgn-2052568), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and interest cover from the five supplied filings, with statements in USD thousands as printed and money tables in US$m. No credit recommendation is made here.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net leverage on reported EBITDA fell from 8.79x at FY2024 to 2.27x at 2026-09-30, first through IPO debt repayment and then through earnings growth that includes acquired businesses, shifting creditor risk to integration and cash conversion.
Basis: calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C8; calculation C14; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 172; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26

The issuer states only adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived here, and the choice matters: net leverage is 2.27x on reported EBITDA (2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01) but 1.28x on the issuer's adjusted figure, and share-based and other non-cash compensation explains over half of the gap. Cash interest cover improved to 5.28x on the last twelve months from 1.61x for FY2025, but cash interest is measured net of swap settlements.

Basis: calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C16; calculation C35; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 201; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45
### Key findings

Deleveraging through FY2025 came from repaying debt, not from earnings: net leverage on reported EBITDA fell to 3.83x from 8.79x while reported EBITDA itself fell by 10.03%, because IPO proceeds and cash on hand repaid USD 780.3 million of term loan in September 2025. Adjusted EBITDA rose by 30.14% in the same year, but 72.25% of the rise in add-backs is the larger share-based compensation charge of the IPO year, so the two measures tell different stories.
Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C37; calculation C38; calculation C39; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 172

Net debt has risen again since the year end because of acquisitions, but last-twelve-month reported EBITDA has nearly doubled, so net leverage still fell to 2.27x, or 2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01. Acquisition spending was the largest use of cash in the nine months, ahead of capital expenditure, so the improvement depends on the acquired businesses holding their earnings and on integration going to plan.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C14; calculation C35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–20

Interest cover on cash interest rose to 5.28x from 1.61x because the IPO paydown cut interest, and is 9.32x on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA. The last twelve months include only nine months of interest on the USD 200.0 million incremental term loan drawn on 2026-01-02, and cash interest is net of swap settlements, so cover on a full year of that loan would be lower.
Basis: calculation C16; calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45

Working capital is absorbing cash as revenue scales, and supplier credit is covering part of it: the rise in contract assets used 66.74% of nine-month operating cash flow, while the rise in accounts payable supplied 42.11%. Balance sheet contract liabilities are up 42.00% and accounts payable 78.84% since the year end, by more than the cash flow statement shows, so part of the increase came with acquired businesses and a slowdown in awards would turn this float into a cash drain.
Basis: calculation C40; calculation C41; calculation C31; calculation C32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10

Liquidity is cash plus an undrawn revolver, and letters of credit have grown to USD 30.7 million from USD 5.7 million at the year end, reducing availability on the USD 200.0 million facility. The springing leverage test applies only when revolver usage exceeds 35% of commitments, so the test is not live while the revolver stays undrawn.
Basis: calculation C28; calculation C29; calculation C30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174
### Limitations

Reported EBITDA is a house calculation because the issuer states only adjusted EBITDA, so every reported-basis ratio moves with non-cash items such as share-based compensation and impairments, and leverage conclusions should be read against both measures.
Basis: calculation C7; calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72

The only maturity ladder in the filings is at 2025-12-31 and predates the incremental term loan of 2026-01-02, so debt maturing by year is not established at the latest balance sheet date beyond the term loan maturity of 2031-12-16.

Cash interest paid is stated net of interest rate swap settlements, so interest cover on cash interest cannot be split between interest and hedge cash flows and understates the burden if swap receipts fade.

## Gaps

- The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA in any period, so EBITDA (Reported) is derived from net income, interest, tax and total depreciation and amortization; this restricts every reported-basis leverage and cover ratio to a house calculation, and the severity is Medium. The action that would close it is the issuer's or the lenders' definition of EBITDA.

- The filings print no maturity ladder at 2026-09-30, and the only ladder at 2025-12-31 predates the incremental term loan of 2026-01-02 and the scheduled repayments since; this restricts the debt maturities chart and the principal reconciliation to 2025-12-31, and the severity is Medium. The action is the quarter-end amortisation schedule.

- Cash interest paid is net of interest rate swap settlements in every period and gross interest cash is not stated; this restricts interest cover to a net measure and prevents a split of hedge cash flows, and the severity is Medium. The action is the swap settlement amounts.

- The filings print dashes for some lines in some periods, among them goodwill impairment, long-lived asset impairment, credit agreement amendment fees, loss on debt extinguishment and the cash flow lines for IPO proceeds and Parent distributions; each is shown as not supplied rather than zero, and lines that appear in only one filing, such as revolver borrowings, are shown as not printed in the other. The severity is Low, and a dash should be read as nil only where the issuer says so.

- The estimated cash consideration for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01 is stated, but the acquired company's net debt, cash and earnings are not, so pro forma net leverage excludes its earnings and may overstate leverage; the severity is Medium. The action is the acquisition's financial terms.

- The share repurchase programme authorised on 2026-11-10 has no stated repurchases, so it has no net debt effect in the post-balance-sheet table; the severity is Low. The action is any later repurchase disclosure.

- The ranking and security of the acquisition promissory notes and finance lease liabilities are not stated and the guarantors are not named, so those facilities are left out of the debt stack; the severity is Low. The action is the guarantor schedule and the notes' terms.
- The revolver maturity of 2030-09-22 is stated in the annual report only and the quarterly reports do not repeat it; the severity is Low. The action is confirmation from the credit agreement.

- No discrete fourth quarter of 2025 is reported, so Q4 2025 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA are calculated and a reported-basis EBITDA for that quarter is not constructed; the severity is Low. The action is the fourth-quarter release.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Legence is a Blackstone-backed building-services group growing quickly through acquisitions and data-centre work, so creditors gain scale and a larger order book but rely on a sponsor-influenced board, unremediated reporting-control weaknesses and the execution of new acquisitions.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 248; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation C13

Blackstone-associated holders owned about 61% of the voting stock in March 2026 and have since sold shares, so their present control is not established, and they have pledged their holdings under margin loans. The IPO repaid USD 780.3 million of term loan after a debt-funded distribution to the sponsor in 2024, but a new USD 150.0 million buyback authorisation and the pace of acquisitions show capital allocation moving from deleveraging to growth and returns.
### Key findings

Revenue is concentrating in one end market and in project work: data centers and technology supplied 42.7% of 2025 revenue and 62.6% of the nine months of 2026, and new building work rose to 61.1% of nine-month revenue from about 40% in 2025. The Maintenance & Service line, the closest to recurring revenue, fell from 12.95% to 10.03% of revenue, so earnings now depend more on the timing of large projects in one sector.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C1; calculation C2

The order book supports near-term revenue but is partly bought and its momentum is easing: backlog rose 77.24% year on year, the filing attributes the rise in backlog and awarded contracts to the Bowers acquisition as well as new awards, and the quarterly book-to-bill ratio slipped to 1.2x from 1.5x while staying above 1.0x. A pipeline that depends on acquired work and on one end market's capital programmes leaves cash flow less visible than the headline backlog suggests.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 75; calculation C13

Sponsor control is loosening, but the sponsor's remaining stake is pledged and its present percentage is not stated. The sponsor vehicles held about 61% of voting shares on 2026-03-24, and share counts imply 46.67% on 2026-11-09 after the April 2026 secondary offering, assuming no other transfers, which is below the 50% level at which the charter lets Blackstone nominate a majority of directors. Lower ownership weakens the sponsor's incentive to support the company and raises the chance of further sell-downs, and both vehicles have pledged all their shares and units under margin loans, so a sponsor-level default could force a sale of the controlling block.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 211; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 248; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 250; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C19

Cash leaves the group toward the sponsor through the tax receivable agreement and through sponsor-linked debt: the liability rose 65.21% since the year end to reflect the April 2026 exchanges, it requires payment of 85% of net cash tax savings, and sponsor-associated lenders hold 8.81% of long-term debt. These flows compete with debt service for cash and mean that amendments and voting under the credit agreement involve parties aligned with the sponsor.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 110; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C23; calculation C24

The sponsor's behaviour is mixed rather than extractive: it took a USD 301.6 million distribution in 2024 funded by a USD 315.0 million incremental term loan, which absorbed 95.75% of that loan, but the 2025 IPO then repaid USD 780.3 million of term loan, and the sponsor's sell-downs are secondary sales that take no cash out of the company. We assign a Medium sponsor and governance risk level, driven by the 2024 distribution and the pledge of shares, with the IPO deleveraging and a board of five independent directors out of six as counterweights.

Reporting controls remain a live governance weakness: management and the auditor identified material weaknesses in information-technology access controls and journal-entry review, still unremediated at 2026-09-30, and an auditor attestation on internal control is first required for the 2026 annual report. Until remediated, covenant certificates and the reported earnings that feed them carry more risk of error than a normally controlled issuer.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the cautious view is deleveraging and diversification of ownership: the IPO repaid USD 780.3 million of term loan, five of six directors are independent, the sponsor is selling rather than adding to its stake, and backlog and awarded contracts rose 92.49% year on year. The view would improve if the material weaknesses are remediated and attested for 2026, if book-to-bill returns to 1.5x, and if the new buyback is funded from cash flow rather than borrowing. It would worsen if the sponsor sells down further and the credit agreement treats a change of control as a default, or if acquisitions continue to be paid for with the term loan.
### Limitations

- The sponsor's voting power after the April 2026 secondary offering is not stated, so the conclusion that its control is loosening rests on share-count arithmetic and would change if a later filing states a different percentage.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 248; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C19

- No credit agreement, stockholders agreement or limited liability company agreement was supplied, so the effect of a lower sponsor stake on change-of-control and restricted-payment terms is not established, and the distribution-risk view would change on reading them.

- Earnings and cash flow of the 2026 acquisitions are not stated apart from consolidated results, so growth cannot be split between organic and acquired, and the conclusion on the quality of backlog growth would change with that split.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The initial public offering completed on 2025-09-15 and converted the sponsor-owned borrower into a listed holding company with an Up-C structure; net proceeds of USD 780.2 million and cash on hand prepaid USD 780.3 million of term loan, and the term loan margin fell by 0.25 percentage points. On 2025-10-30 the credit agreement was amended to extend the term loan maturity to 2031-12-16 and to replace the USD 90.0 million revolver with a USD 200.0 million revolver maturing 2030-09-22.

In 2026 the group used new debt and stock to buy Bowers, Metrix and then CTI: Bowers closed on 2026-01-02 with total consideration of USD 426.68 million and was partly financed by a USD 200.0 million incremental term loan, Metrix closed on 2026-03-01, and CTI closed on 2026-11-01 for estimated consideration of USD 90.0 million cash and 256,411 Class A shares. The term loan was repriced on 2026-05-27 to a margin 0.25 percentage points lower, with a further 0.25 percentage points after ratings upgrades.

The sponsor vehicles sold stock in secondary offerings on 2025-12-16 and 2026-04-09 without proceeds to the company, and on 2026-11-10 the board authorised a USD 150.0 million share repurchase programme with no termination date.

- The filings do not state the sponsor vehicles' voting power after the April 2026 secondary offering, so the control conclusion rests on share-count arithmetic; this restricts any statement on board-nomination rights and controlled-company status, and the severity is High. - The earnings and cash flow of the acquired businesses are not stated apart from consolidated results, so organic growth and the quality of backlog growth cannot be separated from acquired growth; the severity is Medium. The action is acquired-business revenue and EBITDA.

- Sponsor management, monitoring or advisory fees and the terms of the sponsor margin loans are not stated; this leaves value leakage and forced-sale risk unquantified, and the severity is Medium. The action is the related-party and sponsor disclosures.
- The top-ten client share and the fixed-price share of revenue are not quantified; the severity is Low. The action is customer concentration detail from management.
- The remediation date for the material weaknesses is not stated; the severity is Medium. The action is the attestation in the 2026 annual report.

spans.text: # Fundamental credit of Legence Corp. (lgn-2052568)
## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Legence Corp. (lgn-2052568), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: business and revenue durability, margins, cash conversion, liquidity, leverage tolerance, refinancing, financial policy, a qualitative downside path and monitoring triggers, from the supplied filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance findings. No rating, security recommendation or covenant conclusion is drawn.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Legence Corp. for the fiscal year ended 31 December 2025 | 2026-03-30 (date signed; the first-quarter report's exhibit list gives the same filing date) | 51dc065b4728d53abfadd26e7a544b5e8afa84ae0d38cfe57ccdd1cae9a4ba25 | Business model, competition, contracts, supply, labour, risk factors, FY2025 cash flow and subcontractor and equipment cost. |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_lgn-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Legence Corp. for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 | 2026-05-14 (date signed) | e9bb19a3ee6e67552e9c2e2a2db4c61621dd70d771e80363fc95d69bd81a80bd | Not drawn on beyond the figures carried by the Financial foundation findings. |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_lgn-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Legence Corp. for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 | 2026-08-13 (date signed) | 5663e478749a37f05ecffc8c145485144ab952d3f1330a50222ed966ae9935ba | Rating upgrades and the term loan margin step-down as first reported. |

| 424B4_2024-12-31_lgn-20241231.htm.jsonl | Prospectus under Rule 424(b)(4) for the initial public offering of Class A common stock of Legence Corp. | 2025-09-11 (prospectus date; the supplied file name carries 2024-12-31) | 65389676403a6d4dfa57c216a53333cae3fea6fcf986c17e10e3c24bee694310 | Pre-offering background only; not used for current terms. |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | Handoff of the Source readiness module for this run | 2026-11-18 | d541366fd6a2ba0511d4f8797be030349e1b87952d6758c0dd6a61eb176e5002 | Source set, perimeter, and the limits on legal documents, rating levels and market inputs. |

| Financial foundation (CP-1) | Handoff of the Financial foundation module for this run | 2026-11-18 | 9d32222e57ba4d14de805c756c29e9a206370d814085fb6c6c45cc228e19848e | Statements, net debt, leverage, interest cover, liquidity, debt terms and the pro forma adjustment for the acquisition of 2026-11-01. |

| Business & governance (CP-1A) | Handoff of the Business & governance module for this run | 2026-11-18 | cd634b1fb85c1339d86f8bf196a290c99a49ad00e9b77402c9d89d987820ee77 | Ownership and control, sponsor behaviour, tax receivable agreement, related-party debt and internal control status. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Legence's fundamental credit profile is adequate and improving, with moderate leverage and covered near-term cash needs, but it rests on one cyclical end market and on acquired growth, so creditors bear the risk of a data-centre construction slowdown.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3

Net leverage is 2.27x on reported earnings, or 2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01, and cash plus the undrawn revolver covers identified near-term calls 3.02x. Data centers supplied 86.26% of the nine-month revenue increase, while the new buyback authorisation and the pace of acquisitions show financial policy moving from repayment toward growth and shareholder returns.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C3; calculation C30
### Key findings

Revenue durability is the weakest dimension because growth is concentrated in data-centre construction. Data centers and technology supplied 62.6% of nine-month 2026 revenue against 39.2% a year earlier and 86.26% of the revenue increase, while all other end markets together grew 22.39%. New building is now 61.1% of revenue, the vast majority of contracts are fixed-price, and the bulk of performance comes late in a project, so a client deferral cuts revenue and raises working-capital needs at once. Maintenance & Service, the most recurring line, fell to 10.03% of revenue from 13.28% a year earlier, so little of the base repeats under contract.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C51

Contracted visibility equals about two thirds of a year's revenue but is partly bought. Backlog is 77.24% higher than a year ago, and 65% to 75% of it is expected to convert within 12 months, which equals 61.41% to 70.86% of last-twelve-month revenue. The issuer attributes part of the increase to the Bowers acquisition, and the quarterly book-to-bill ratio, which excludes acquired additions, slipped to 1.2x from 1.5x. That is still above 1.0x, so organic awards remain ahead of revenue by a narrowing margin, and a ratio below 1.0x would signal falling revenue.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 73–75; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C47; calculation C6; calculation C7

Adjusted margins are holding through a mix shift, but the reported cushion is thin. Adjusted EBITDA margin is 12.5% against 11.7% a year earlier, yet nine-month gross margin fell to 18.89% from 21.43% because the lower-margin Installation & Maintenance segment rose to 84.14% of revenue from 69.46%, while that segment's own margin rose to 16.58% from 15.67% and Engineering & Consulting fell to 31.13% from 34.51% on higher compensation, a shift toward project management and lower design margins. Reported EBITDA is 6.99% of last-twelve-month revenue against 12.34% on the issuer's adjusted basis, and because fixed-price contracts and wages are the largest costs, overruns land directly on creditors' cash flow.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 83–84; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C16; calculation C17

Cash conversion is good but flattered by timing. Free cash flow after capital expenditure for the last twelve months equals 98.18% of reported EBITDA and 55.59% of adjusted EBITDA, yet FY2025 included a working-capital inflow while the nine months of 2026 absorbed an outflow, cash taxes paid rose 147.62%, and the issuer expects capital expenditure to increase for fabrication capacity. Conversion therefore depends on customer advances and supplier credit continuing as revenue scales, and a slowdown would reverse both.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 124–125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C27

Liquidity covers identified near-term calls about three times, and the only maintenance covenant is not live. Cash plus the USD 169.3 million undrawn revolver covers the USD 90.0 million cash price of the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01, deferred consideration, current debt and the current tax receivable payment 3.02x, or 1.60x if the whole USD 150.0 million buyback authorisation were also used. The springing 8.50x first lien net leverage test applies only when revolver usage passes USD 70.0 million and letters of credit already use USD 30.7 million of that, so the test is not live. Net debt over adjusted EBITDA of 1.28x is only an orientation, because the covenant uses the executed definition of consolidated pro forma adjusted EBITDA, which the filings describe only in summary, so covenant headroom is not calculated.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 67; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C29; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C32; calculation C33; calculation C34

Leverage is moderate, but financial policy has turned from repayment to growth and returns, and the sponsor's pledged stake adds control risk. Net leverage fell from 8.79x at FY2024 to 2.27x at 2026-09-30 (2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01) after the IPO repaid USD 780.3 million of term loan, but the group has since drawn a USD 200.0 million incremental term loan, completed three acquisitions and authorised a USD 150.0 million buyback. The credit agreement also lets the borrower add pari passu debt, subject to conditions, while first lien net leverage is no greater than 5.25x and, by management's estimate at 2025-12-31, about USD 1.4 billion of junior secured and USD 1.5 billion of unsecured debt, so the current ratio does not bind financial policy. Blackstone-linked holders owned about 61% of the votes in March 2026 and an indicative 46.67% in November 2026 on share-count arithmetic, they have pledged all their shares, and the tax receivable agreement and sponsor-linked lenders align cash and votes with the sponsor rather than with creditors.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47

Refinancing risk is low before 2030, but interest-rate protection rolls over within weeks and the margin depends on ratings. The revolver matures on 2030-09-22 and the term loan on 2031-12-16, while swaps covering 79.27% of the term loan expire on 2026-12-31 and forward swaps cover 60.59% from that date, so 39.41% floats unhedged above a 0.75% SOFR floor. The June 2026 rating upgrades by two agencies triggered a further cut of 0.25 percentage points in the term loan margin, which depends on ratings being maintained, and the rating levels themselves are not stated.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 173–174; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C36; calculation C37; calculation C38
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the cautious view is that deleveraging and cash generation are reported, not forecast: net leverage fell to 2.27x (2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01), last-twelve-month free cash flow was 98.18% of reported EBITDA, two agencies upgraded the company in June 2026, and the average relationship with the ten largest clients is 23 years with no client above 10% of revenue. Those facts lower single-name risk and make a quick liquidity squeeze unlikely. The view would improve if book-to-bill stays above 1.0x while the data-centre share stops rising, if working-capital float persists without acquired help, if the control weaknesses are remediated, and if the buyback is paid from free cash flow. It would worsen if revolver usage passed USD 70.0 million, if book-to-bill fell below 1.0x, if the sponsor's margin lenders forced a sale of its controlling block, or if reported net leverage rose back toward 3.83x.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 155; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 74; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C21
### Limitations

- Covenant headroom is not calculable because the executed credit agreement and its definition of consolidated pro forma adjusted EBITDA are not supplied, so the conclusion that the springing test is far from live rests on revolver usage alone and would change if usage rose above USD 70.0 million or if the covenant's pro forma adjusted EBITDA proved well below the issuer's adjusted figure.

- The filings name no rating levels or outlooks, only the dates of two upgrades, so the improvement in refinancing access is read from the margin step-down alone and would weaken if the upgraded levels still sit deep in speculative grade.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66

- Revenue is split by end market but not by client or project, so the concentration conclusion rests on the end-market total and would soften if data-centre revenue is spread across many clients and sites, or harden if a few carry most of it.

- No management guidance, sector forecast or peer data is supplied, so the outlook extends the current backlog and the issuer's own risk statements and the comparison with other leveraged building-services issuers is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Strengths and weaknesses

The four main supports are liquidity and maturities, cash generation, falling funding cost and contracted visibility; the five main constraints are data-centre concentration, acquisition-led financial policy, the quality of reported earnings, dependence on working-capital float and sponsor-linked claims on cash.

Liquidity and maturities are the main support. The undrawn USD 200.0 million revolver (USD 169.3 million available after letters of credit) and cash cover identified near-term calls 3.02x, no debt falls due before the revolver matures on 2030-09-22 apart from USD 10.0 million of yearly term loan amortisation, small acquisition notes and finance leases, and the only maintenance covenant is untested, so a liquidity-driven default over the next 12 to 24 months is unlikely.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 173–174; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C30

Cash generation supports debt service. Free cash flow after capital expenditure over the last twelve months equals 98.18% of reported EBITDA, and reported EBITDA covers cash interest 5.28x, so debt service does not depend on refinancing; the caveat is that FY2025 conversion included a working-capital inflow and the interest figure is net of swap settlements.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C21; calculation C23

Funding cost and leverage are falling. Net leverage fell from 8.79x at FY2024 to 2.27x at 2026-09-30 (2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01), and the term loan margin moved from SOFR plus 2.25% to SOFR plus 1.75% after the May 2026 amendment and the June 2026 upgrades, which lowers the interest burden and widens refinancing options.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66

Contracted visibility and client relationships limit near-term revenue risk. Backlog is 77.24% higher than a year ago, 65% to 75% of it converts within 12 months, the ten largest clients have a 23-year average relationship and no client exceeds 10% of revenue, so next year's revenue is largely contracted although the backlog is partly acquired.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 155; calculation C47; calculation C6; calculation C7

Concentration in data-centre construction is the main constraint. Data centers and technology supplied 62.6% of nine-month revenue and 86.26% of its increase, clients may reduce or terminate contracts at any time, and utility or water shortages can make data-centre clients defer projects, so a pause in that capital cycle would cut revenue and margins together and shorten the backlog's life.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C3

Acquisition-led financial policy is the second constraint. ### Company description and credit linkage

Legence designs, installs and maintains heating, cooling, electrical and plumbing systems for mission-critical buildings such as data centers, laboratories, hospitals and universities. It reports two segments, Engineering & Consulting at 15.86% of nine-month 2026 revenue and Installation & Maintenance at 84.14%, and most jobs other than maintenance finish within nine months. Acquisitions have changed the business in 2026: the Bowers acquisition alone explains about one third of the rise in Installation & Maintenance gross profit.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; calculation C46; calculation C14

This model gives cash-flow visibility through backlog but little recurring revenue: Maintenance & Service, mostly cost-plus, is 10.03% of revenue, while the vast majority of contracts are fixed-price. The mission-critical nature of the buildings supports client retention and bonding access, but revenue follows client capital budgets, so debt service rests on project execution and billing timing, not on a contracted annuity.

### Ownership and group structure

Legence Corp. is a listed holding company that consolidates Legence Holdings LLC, the borrower under the credit agreement, in an Up-C structure; the term loan and revolver are secured by a lien on substantially all assets of the borrower and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, and guarantors are not named. Blackstone-linked vehicles held about 61% of the votes in March 2026 and an indicative 46.67% in November 2026, which is below the 50% level at which Blackstone may nominate a majority of the board, and they have pledged all their shares and units under margin loans.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

For creditors this means the sponsor's influence is declining but not gone, a forced sale by its lenders could change control, and the tax receivable agreement and related-party lenders give the sponsor claims on cash beside the credit agreement. The 2024 distribution of USD 301.6 million, funded by a USD 315.0 million term loan, shows the sponsor has extracted value before, while the IPO repayment of USD 780.3 million and sell-downs without company proceeds show support since; Business & governance rates the sponsor and governance risk as Medium.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is transactional, cyclical and concentrated, not recurring. Volume follows client capital programmes, led by data centers and technology (62.6% of nine-month revenue), with new building at 61.1%, and the issuer says downturns bring greater price competition and lower revenue and profit. Pricing power is limited on fixed-price work, where scope changes are billed but base prices are fixed, although tariffs on internationally procured materials are passed to clients and the issuer says it typically takes no exposure to equipment price increases.

Revenue outside data centers grew 22.39% over nine months, which shows demand in other markets, yet Engineering & Design revenue fell 4.66% and one Engineering & Consulting unit lost new contracts in the second quarter of 2026 as demand for sustainability services fell, and the issuer wrote down goodwill and long-lived assets there. Switching costs and long relationships (23 years on average for the ten largest clients) support retention, yet contracts can be reduced or terminated at any time, so revenue visibility depends on the backlog rather than on contract terms.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure but not under a sharp project slowdown. Wages are the largest cost and the workforce is partly unionised under 44 collective agreements, so labour is semi-fixed. Subcontractor and equipment spending, 40.32% of FY2025 revenue, may be passed to clients as a line item or priced into the job, and the issuer says it typically takes no exposure to equipment price increases, which protects margin against input inflation. Because contracts are fixed-price, errors in labour estimates fall on the company, and the issuer says engineering, project management and maintenance earn higher margins than installation, the line that grew fastest at 162.76% over nine months.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 83–84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C44; calculation C52

Operating leverage works both ways: nine-month gross margin of 18.89% against 21.43% a year earlier fell with mix, while the Installation & Maintenance margin rose to 16.58%, so resilience rests on installation project margins holding. The reported EBITDA margin of 6.99% is the conservative base, while the adjusted margin of 12.34% adds back non-cash compensation, impairments and deal costs, so conclusions on resilience should use the reported margin and treat the adjusted one as an upper bound.

### Capital intensity and cash conversion

The business is asset-light but capital expenditure is rising: purchases of property and equipment rose 143.32% over nine months and the issuer expects further increases for fabrication capacity in Installation & Maintenance. Free cash flow of the last twelve months equals 98.18% of reported EBITDA, but FY2025 free cash flow before the working-capital lines was lower than reported, while the nine months of 2026 absorbed a working-capital outflow and cash taxes paid rose 147.62%.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 124–125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation C28; calculation C21; calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C27

EBITDA therefore translates into debt-service cash now, but the translation depends on customer advances and payables, which the nine-month contract liability movement shows can shrink quickly. Capital expenditure is a flexible lever in a slowdown, whereas interest, term loan amortisation of USD 10.0 million a year, operating lease liabilities of USD 163,555 thousand and the tax receivable payments are not, and the deferred consideration due on 2026-12-31 is payable in cash or shares at the company's option.

Claims outside the debt figure add to fixed charges: operating leases, the tax receivable liability, surety bonds of USD 1,346.3 million and customer guarantees of USD 283.6 million, and multiemployer pension plans, to which the group contributed about USD 75.6 million in FY2025 and whose withdrawal liability the issuer says it cannot estimate. Management says it has not incurred material losses on the guarantees, so these claims matter mainly if a slowdown coincides with project losses or a union withdrawal.
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is moderate to high: the issuer competes with national groups such as Comfort Systems USA and Southland Industries and with many small owner-operated firms, and price competition rises in downturns. The issuer says its integrated service offer is an advantage over smaller competitors, but the filings describe no barrier to entry beyond engineering skill, bonding relationships and client ties of 23 years on average, and small owner-operated firms already compete locally, so installation margins are exposed in a slowdown. Substitutes are not evidenced in the filings.

Buyer power is high on large projects because contracts are fixed-price, work is often subcontracted through general contractors and architects, and clients can reduce or terminate contracts at any time, offset by long relationships and no client above 10% of revenue. Supplier power is low for equipment and materials, which come from many vendors, with tariffs and equipment costs passed to clients, but high for scarce skilled labour, where shortages could raise wages and third-party costs.
### Macro and policy factors

Three outside factors change the credit view. Interest rates and the construction cycle drive client capital budgets and the cost of the floating-rate term loan, so rate moves reach cash flow through both the hedge expiry on 2026-12-31 and client demand. Trade policy and tariffs raise material costs and delay supply; the issuer says tariffs on internationally procured materials are passed to clients, which protects margins but can slow projects. Technology investment in data centers, and the availability of water or other utility services at their sites, set the pace of the largest end market.

### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is adequate and improving. The main supports are moderate leverage (2.27x reported, 2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01), cash generation of 98.18% of reported EBITDA, and covered near-term calls. The main constraints are revenue concentration, thin reported earnings (a 6.99% margin), acquisition-driven leverage and sponsor-linked claims. The trend is better on leverage and interest cover, which rose to 5.28x on reported EBITDA, and worse on concentration, which rose from 39.2% to 62.6% in a year.

Missing datapoints that would move the profile are the executed credit agreement and its definition of consolidated pro forma adjusted EBITDA, the rating levels, revenue by client or project, the earnings and net debt of acquired businesses including the one completed on 2026-11-01, and any management guidance.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the outlook is supportive for revenue and cautious for cash. Backlog conversion, the Bowers business and the margin step-down support revenue and interest cost, while the swap expiry on 2026-12-31, the deferred consideration due on that date, capital expenditure for fabrication capacity and a cash price of USD 90.0 million for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01 absorb cash, and a first auditor attestation on internal control is due for 2026. Book-to-bill of 1.2x says awards are still ahead of revenue.

Over three to five years the outlook depends on how long data-centre and life-science construction stays strong, because that decides how much of the installed work turns into repeat maintenance revenue, and on how sponsor ownership evolves before the 2030 revolver and 2031 term loan maturities. No management guidance or sector forecast is supplied, so this horizon is not established beyond the issuer's own risk statements. Sector tailwinds are technology investment and building-efficiency demand; headwinds are utility constraints at data-centre sites, tariffs, skilled labour shortages and higher rates. Company tailwinds are backlog, bonding access and acquisition integration; company headwinds are the sponsor's pledged stake, the tax receivable agreement and the shift of policy toward the buyback.
### Qualitative downside scenario

The realistic downside starts with data-centre clients deferring projects, for example because utility services such as water are unavailable at a site or because a client's own capital budget is cut. The first operational break is slower backlog conversion on fixed-price new-building work, where most performance comes late in a project, with the labour force and fabrication capacity already in place; book-to-bill falling below 1.0x would confirm it. Revenue and installation margins fall together, and because wages are the largest cost and many employees are unionised, costs adjust slowly.

Cash then falls faster than EBITDA because the float reverses: contract liabilities and payables, which grew 42.00% and 78.84% since the year end, would shrink while contract assets, up 97.47%, take longer to bill, and surety bonds of USD 1,346.3 million and letters of credit of USD 30.7 million tie up bonding capacity and revolver availability. Liquidity absorbs this: cash plus the undrawn revolver covers identified calls 3.02x, capital expenditure and the USD 150.0 million buyback are discretionary, and deferred consideration can be paid in shares.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C42; calculation C39; calculation C30

Leverage is the slower channel. Reported EBITDA would have to fall 33.07% before pro forma net leverage of 2.56x returned to the 3.83x of FY2025, and the springing test applies only if revolver usage passes USD 70.0 million, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in a moderate slowdown. A change of control would add a further call, because the tax receivable agreement ends early on one and requires a termination payment whose amount is not stated. A severe, prolonged freeze combined with a sponsor margin-loan default, a loss of the rating-linked margin step-down and weak integration of acquired businesses would be needed to threaten debt service, and the observable triggers are book-to-bill below 1.0x, revolver usage rising, negative working-capital cash flow and a sponsor sale.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C35; calculation C33
### Overall credit view

Overall, Legence presents an adequate business profile supported by backlog, long client relationships and bonding access, but credit quality is constrained by data-centre concentration, acquisition-led growth, thin reported earnings and sponsor-linked claims on cash. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow was 98.18% of reported EBITDA, though it depends on working-capital float. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the data-centre cycle, the ratings that underpin the margin step-down and the covenant staying untested; no large debt maturity falls due before 2030. The primary downside path is a pause in data-centre construction that reverses working-capital float while acquisition and sponsor claims keep cash leaving. Against typical leveraged building-services issuers the profile cannot be ranked because no peer data is supplied. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, the rating levels, revenue by client, and the earnings and net debt of acquired businesses. Top risk: concentration in one end market funded in part by acquisitions.

## Gaps

- The executed credit agreement and its definition of consolidated pro forma adjusted EBITDA are not supplied, so covenant headroom under the springing 8.50x test cannot be calculated; this restricts the liquidity and downside conclusions to revolver usage, and the severity is Medium. The action is the executed agreement and the quarterly compliance certificate.

- The filings name no rating levels or outlooks, only the dates of two 2026 upgrades and a rating-linked margin step-down; this restricts the refinancing assessment and any rating-transition view, and the severity is Medium. The action is the agencies' current reports.

- Revenue is not split by client or project, so the share of data-centre revenue carried by the largest clients and sites is not established; this restricts the concentration conclusion, and the severity is Medium. The action is client-level concentration detail from management.

- No management guidance, sector forecast or peer data is supplied, so the three-to-five-year outlook and the comparison with other leveraged building-services issuers are not established; the severity is Low. The action is management guidance and a peer set.

- The planned amount and timing of capital expenditure for fabrication capacity are not stated beyond an expected increase, so free cash flow after that spending cannot be projected; the severity is Low. The action is a capital expenditure plan.

- The amount of the termination payment that the tax receivable agreement requires on a change of control is not stated, so the call a sale of the controlling block would add cannot be sized; the severity is Medium. The action is the agreement or a later disclosure of the termination estimate.

- The funded status of the multiemployer pension plans and any withdrawal liability are not estimable by the issuer, so claims outside debt from union plans cannot be sized; the severity is Low. The action is plan funding notices.

- The cash flow, net debt and earnings of the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01 are not stated, so pro forma leverage excludes its earnings and the liquidity cover uses only its estimated cash price; the severity is Low. The action is the acquisition's financial terms.

- Interest paid is stated only net of swap settlements and the filings give no all-in term loan rate or SOFR level at the quarter end, so the cash cost of the swap roll on 2026-12-31 cannot be measured; the severity is Low. The action is gross interest and settlement amounts.
